fatal_errors: Changing composition to vary atomic-size mismatch also changes bonding, elastic modulus, stacking-fault energy, chemical short-range order, and phase stability, so the design does not uniquely isolate lattice distortion.

XRD peak broadening is not a specific measure of static lattice distortion because crystallite size, dislocation microstrain, compositional heterogeneity, and instrumental broadening can produce the same signal.
explanation: The hypothesis directly addresses HEA hardness and strength and proposes a controlled baseline, boundaries, measurements, and an explicit falsification rule. It is therefore a scientifically plausible alternative. However, it does not reconstruct the targeted powder-processing comparison: it omits high-energy ball milling, SPS, their specified process window, nanocrystalline grain refinement, densification, the stabilized FCC/BCC mixture, and the cast-alloy baseline. Its mechanism captures only the solid-solution component of the target, whereas the target attributes the high properties to synergy among Hall–Petch strengthening, milling-induced dislocation density, solid-solution strengthening, and reduced porosity. It also makes only qualitative outcome predictions and supplies no empirical evidence or target values such as 675 HV and 1894 MPa. The experiment is reasonably falsifiable, but causal attribution remains vulnerable to composition-dependent confounders and nonspecific interpretation of XRD broadening.
